/itineraryStops/2/highlights/0.source_en: **72.5-m skywalk, ~20 m above the sea** — opened August 2017, FREE

/itineraryStops/2/highlights/1.source_en: Named for the five **daritdol 'stepping-stone' reefs** visible below the deck

/itineraryStops/2/highlights/2.source_en: **Glass-floor section** at the seaward end (shoe covers provided)

/itineraryStops/2/highlights/3.source_en: **Cheongsapo Twin Lighthouses** (red + white) a short stroll away

/itineraryStops/2/highlights/4.source_en: Cheongsapo is one of Busan's **eight scenic views** — a working fishing village

/itineraryStops/2/smartNotes/tip.source_en: Windy days close the deck occasionally — the guide checks conditions and reorders the Cheongsapo cluster if needed

/itineraryStops/2/smartNotes/facilities.source_en: Cafes and seafood stalls in Cheongsapo village below

/itineraryStops/2/whyOnRoute.source_en: **The free thrill between the temple and the capsule.** Daritdol gives the day its over-the-sea moment — a glass floor with swell rolling underneath — without a ticket, and it sits directly on the Cheongsapo cliff so it chains into the Sky Capsule boarding just minutes away. Seeing the coastline from the fixed skywalk first makes the moving capsule view read differently ten minutes later.

/itineraryStops/2/convenience/parking.source_en: Coach stop at Cheongsapo village; short walk to the deck

/itineraryStops/2/description.source_en: The **Cheongsapo Daritdol Observatory (청사포 다릿돌전망대)** is a **72.5-meter skywalk curving out over the sea about 20 meters above the water**, opened in August 2017 on the coastal cliff between Cheongsapo and Songjeong. Its name comes from the **daritdol — the five 'stepping-stone' reef rocks** that dot the sea below the deck, said to step toward the horizon like a bridge. The far section of the deck floor is **glass**, with shoe covers provided to protect (and trust!) the panes as the swell rolls beneath your feet. Admission is **free**. Back at the village, the **Cheongsapo Twin Lighthouses** (one red, one white) and the little station crosswalk made famous by its Slam-Dunk-style anime frame are a short stroll away.

/itineraryStops/2/visitBasics/hours.source_en: Open access; observatory staffed roughly 09:00–18:00 (season/weather dependent)

/itineraryStops/2/visitBasics/closed.source_en: May close temporarily in high wind or storm conditions

/itineraryStops/2/visitBasics/walking.source_en: Flat walk-out on the deck; a short slope from the village

/itineraryStops/2/visitBasics/admission.source_en: FREE (shoe covers provided for the glass section)

/itineraryStops/3/timeUsed/1.source_en: Sky Capsule ride Cheongsapo → Mipo (~35 min)

/itineraryStops/3/highlights/0.source_en: **Pastel 4-seat capsules on an elevated coastal rail** — Blueline Park's signature ride (opened 2020)

/itineraryStops/3/highlights/1.source_en: **Cheongsapo → Mipo, 2.3 km / ~30 min**, sea views the whole way

/itineraryStops/3/highlights/2.source_en: **Ticket included or excluded — your choice at booking** (per-capsule pricing ≈ ₩30,000 for 2 / ₩39,000 for 3 / ₩44,000 for 4, one-way)

/itineraryStops/3/highlights/3.source_en: Non-riders: **free Green Railway boardwalk** along the same coast, or the coach to Mipo

/itineraryStops/3/highlights/4.source_en: The ride ends where lunch begins — Mipo is a short walk from Haeundae's food streets

/itineraryStops/3/highlights/5.source_en: Runs in normal rain; pauses only in high wind

/itineraryStops/3/smartNotes/tip.source_en: Sunset and weekend slots sell out 1–2 weeks ahead — choose the ticket-included option at booking and we reserve them for you

/itineraryStops/3/smartNotes/facilities.source_en: Cafes and convenience store at Mipo plaza; ticket kiosks at both stations

/itineraryStops/3/whyOnRoute.source_en: **The ride that is also the transfer.** Boarding at Cheongsapo right after the skywalk means the capsule carries you down the exact coastline you just looked out over — and it deposits you at Mipo, where the coach and the lunch streets are already waiting. Nothing about the day detours for it: skip the ticket and the coach or the free boardwalk cover the same leg.

/itineraryStops/3/convenience/parking.source_en: Coach meets the group at Mipo station plaza

/itineraryStops/3/convenience/restroom.source_en: At both Cheongsapo and Mipo stations

/itineraryStops/3/description.source_en: The **Sky Capsule** is the signature ride of **Haeundae Blueline Park**, the 2020 eco-redevelopment of the disused Donghae Nambu coastal railway: **pastel 4-seat cabins gliding 2.3 km along an elevated rail 7–10 meters above the coastline** between Cheongsapo and Mipo, with the sea on one side the whole way (~30 minutes). We board at **Cheongsapo and ride toward Mipo**, where the coach is already waiting — so the ride doubles as the day's transfer down the coast. **The capsule ticket is optional and chosen at booking**: with the ticket-included option we pre-reserve capsules for your group (pricing is per capsule: about ₩30,000 for 2 / ₩39,000 for 3 / ₩44,000 for 4, one-way); with the base option you can walk the **free Green Railway boardwalk** — the award-winning 2.3 km wooden coastal path under the same rail — or simply ride the coach to Mipo.

/itineraryStops/3/visitBasics/hours.source_en: ≈ 09:30–18:30 (extended into the evening in peak season)

/itineraryStops/3/visitBasics/walking.source_en: Flat station platforms; boardwalk alternative is 2.3 km (~30 min) on wood decking

/itineraryStops/3/visitBasics/admission.source_en: Per capsule, one-way: ≈ ₩30,000 (2 pax) / ₩39,000 (3) / ₩44,000 (4) — included-ticket option available at booking
